newsitem.title: USA: House gives final approval to budget deal.
newsitem.headline: House gives final approval to budget deal.

text.p: The House Thursday gave final approval to a historic budget agreement which aims to bring the federal deficit to zero by 2002 and cut taxes by net $85 billion over five years.
The House approved the final version of the budget on a bipartisan vote of 327 to 97 and sent it to the Senate where it was also expected to be approved.

The budget agreement does not go to President Clinton for his signature but was worked out with the administration. It serves as a blueprint for spending and tax legislation which will be crafted this summer and those bills will need his approval to become law.

Wednesday, a key panel took the first concrete action to translate the budget into law. The House Ways and Means health subcommittee unanimously approved a broad plan to restructure the Medicare programme and cut spending by $115 billion over five years.

The House Ways and Means Committee is expected to start work Next week on the total $135 billion five-year tax cut. About $50 billion of the tax reduction is to be paid for with an extension of the airline ticket tax and other taxes.

House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, Republican of Ohio, a central player in months of negotiations with the White House, urged his colleagues to adhere to the budget in the face of pressures to revise it in the next months.
